title: Tensorization of a reverse norm inequality
statement: Let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<q<p$ and $0\le\rho\le1$. Suppose that for every nonnegative real-valued function $u$ on the one-dimensional Boolean cube, $M_q(T_\rho u)\ge M_p(u)$. Then for every natural number $n$ and every nonnegative real-valued function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$, where $T_\rho$ is the Walsh–Fourier noise operator and $M_r$ is the extended power mean defined for cube functions.
hypotheses_covered: the reverse mean inequality holds for every nonnegative function on the one-dimensional cube
$f$ is a nonnegative real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional cube
replaced: Let $0<q<p$ and $0\le\rho\le1$. Suppose $M_q(T_\rho u)\ge M_p(u)$ for every nonnegative function $u$ on one bit. Then $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$ for every $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$, where $M_r(u)=(\E|u|^r)^{1/r}$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
